title: UART Transmitter
constraints: 8N1 frames: 1 start bit (0), 8 data bits LSB first, 1 stop bit (1). Each bit lasts exactly 4 clock cycles (CLKS_PER_BIT = 4).
A frame starts on a rising edge that samples `start = 1` while `busy = 0`. `data` is captured at that edge, and the start bit appears in the next cycle.
`busy = 1` for exactly the 40 cycles of the frame. `start` is ignored while busy.
Idle line: `tx = 1`, `busy = 0`. The synchronous reset returns to idle.
hints: Load a 10-bit shift register with `{1'b1, data, 1'b0}` and shift it right, one bit every 4 cycles. `tx` is its LSB.
You need a 2-bit cycle counter (0 – 3) and a 4-bit bit counter (0 – 9).
The frame ends on the edge that completes the 4th cycle of the stop bit. That same edge clears `busy`.

examples.title: one byte
examples.input: start = 1 with data = 0x55 for one edge
examples.expected: tx: 0000 1111 0000 1111 … (LSB first, 4 cycles per bit), 1111 stop, busy = 1 for 40 cycles

examples.title: busy
examples.expected: no effect: the current frame completes unchanged

examples.title: continuous start
examples.expected: frames separated by exactly one idle cycle
